subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should trusted plugins be allowed to synchronously veto all configuration writes, and what redaction, timeout, error, recursion, ordering, and emergency-recovery policy should govern that authority?
rationale: Source proves the extension gap, but granting plugin code control over sensitive configuration persistence and recovery is a permanent security and availability boundary requiring maintainer intent.

options.title: Trusted typed veto
options.body: Add a trusted-plugin-only, timeout-bounded hook at the canonical commit boundary with redacted payloads and a documented recovery bypass.

options.title: Advisory validation event
options.body: Expose pending-change context to plugins but reserve rejection authority for core validation.

options.title: Core-only hardening
options.body: Keep persistence exclusively core-owned and expand built-in provider, schema, preflight, and doctor validation instead.

recommendation.title: Trusted typed veto
recommendation.body: Add a trusted-plugin-only, timeout-bounded hook at the canonical commit boundary with redacted payloads and a documented recovery bypass.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion gives this account the strongest current product and security routing context for the decision.
